The **AWS Snow Family** is a collection of physical hardware appliances designed to securely capture, process, and migrate massive volumes of data into and out of the AWS cloud without relying on internet connectivity. Historically encompassing three models—**Snowcone**, **Snowball**, and **Snowmobile**—the product lineup has shifted dramatically toward cloud-based alternatives like [AWS DataSync](https://aws.amazon.com/datasync/). [[1](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/aws-retires-snowmobile-truck-based-data-transfer-service/), [2](https://community.spiceworks.com/t/aws-snow-family-faqs/944003), [3](https://jayendrapatil.com/aws-snow-family/)]

Learn how the AWS Snow Family enables secure, physical data migrations and edge computing when internet-based transfers are impractical:

Current Hardware Availability & Service Lifecycle

|Device Tier|Maximum Historical Capacity|Local Compute Support|Lifecycle Status|
|---|---|---|---|
|**AWS Snowcone**|8 TB – 14 TB|AWS IoT Greengrass & EC2 (2 vCPUs)|**Discontinued** (November 12, 2024); support ended November 12, 2025.|
|**AWS Snowball Edge**|80 TB – 210 TB|EC2 & Lambda (up to 104 vCPUs / 416GB RAM)|**Active** (Commercial support scheduled to conclude on **December 31, 2026**).|
|**AWS Snowmobile**|100 PB per truck|None (Data transfer only)|**Retired** (April 2024).|

Deep Dive into the Models

1. AWS Snowball Edge (Active)

Snowball Edge is a suitcase-sized, ruggedized appliance intended for petabyte-scale data transfers and complex local data processing in disconnected environments (like ships, factories, or mining sites). [[1](https://aws.amazon.com/compare/snow-family-and-snowball/), [2](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7yOOCmZxmog&t=111)]

- **Storage Optimized:** Features up to **210TB of fast NVMe storage** tailored for rapid file migrations and large-scale block storage needs.
- **Compute Optimized:** Packs **104 vCPUs and 416GB of RAM** alongside high-performance local NVMe storage to run containerized microservices and AI/ML workloads at the physical edge.
- **Clustering Capability:** Multiple units can be linked together on-site to create localized high-availability storage pools. [[1](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/storage/aws-snow-device-updates/), [2](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/storage/aws-reinvent-recap-optimize-your-data-migration-with-aws-snow-family/), [3](https://dev.to/clintt/aws-snow-family-875)]

2. AWS Snowcone (Discontinued)

Snowcone was the most compact, ultra-portable member of the family, built roughly the size of a standard lunchbox and weighing 4.5 lbs. It was engineered for severe space- and power-constrained environments, field research deployments, or mounting directly onto drone frames. Data was shipped back manually or synced over weak networks via AWS DataSync. [[1](https://k21academy.com/aws-cloud/aws-snow-family/), [2](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zXyudn7KeZM&t=331), [3](https://community.spiceworks.com/t/aws-snow-family-faqs/944003), [4](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Smd-sOkgieU&t=380)]

3. AWS Snowmobile (Retired)

Snowmobile was an exabyte-scale behemoth consisting of a **45-foot ruggedized shipping container pulled by a semi-trailer truck**. It could swallow up to **100 petabytes of data** directly from on-premises data centers over dedicated high-speed fiber lines. AWS retired the truck fleet in 2024 due to the logistical challenges of managing power, security, and cooling on-site, alongside the emergence of ultra-high-speed network migration alternatives. [[1](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/aws-retires-snowmobile-truck-based-data-transfer-service/), [2](https://k21academy.com/aws-cloud/aws-snow-family/), [3](https://www.heise.de/en/news/Moving-100-petabytes-to-the-cloud-by-truck-Amazon-discontinues-Snowmobile-9689558.html)]

Core Security Principles

Every active device in the Snow Family implements military-grade security controls to ensure data integrity during physical transport:

- **Hardware-Enforced Encryption:** All stored data is continuously locked down using 256-bit encryption managed via the [AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS)](https://aws.amazon.com/kms/). Keys are never stored directly on the device. [[1](https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/devops/aws-snow-family/), [2](https://k21academy.com/aws-cloud/aws-snow-family/)]
- **Tamper Evidence:** Units feature specialized physical enclosures and internal **Trusted Platform Modules (TPM)** to detect and log physical intrusion attempts. [[1](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/storage/aws-reinvent-recap-optimize-your-data-migration-with-aws-snow-family/), [2](https://k21academy.com/aws-cloud/aws-snow-family/)]
- **Cryptographic Erasure:** Once data is successfully ingested into your Amazon S3 buckets at an AWS facility, the physical device undergoes a multi-pass, NIST-compliant cryptographic wipe before returning to circulation. [[1](https://aws.amazon.com/snowball/), [2](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7yOOCmZxmog&t=111)]
